summary.text: The Cosmic Background Explorer, or COBE, was a NASA satellite that studied the cosmic microwave background from 1989 to 1993.
It found that the background has a near-perfect black-body spectrum and very faint anisotropies, two key pieces of evidence for the Big Bang theory.
It was the second cosmic microwave background satellite, following RELIKT-1, and was followed by WMAP and Planck.

facts.label: Successors
facts.value: WMAP and then the Planck spacecraft

items.prompt: COBE's measurements gave two key pieces of evidence for the Big Bang. Which pair was it?

options.label: A near-perfect black-body spectrum and very faint anisotropies
A perfectly smooth sky and a fixed spectrum
Bright hot spots and a rising temperature
A radio signal from each galaxy and a steady glow

items.explain: COBE showed the background has a near-perfect black-body spectrum and also very faint anisotropies.

items.prompt: The Nobel committee called a project the starting point for cosmology as a precision science. Which project?

options.label: The Planck spacecraft
The Challenger Space Shuttle program
The Cosmic Background Explorer
The Infrared Astronomical Satellite

items.explain: According to the committee, the COBE project can be regarded as the starting point for cosmology as a precision science.

items.prompt: COBE's launch plan changed after a Shuttle disaster grounded the fleet. What happened to the launch?

options.label: It was cancelled and the satellite never flew
It was moved to a second Shuttle mission in 1990
It went up with a Russian rocket from a foreign site
A redesigned satellite flew on a Delta rocket in 1989

items.explain: The Challenger explosion delayed the Shuttle plan, so a redesigned COBE was launched into a Sun-synchronous orbit aboard a Delta launch vehicle in November 1989.

items.prompt: Why was COBE built to spin slowly, at 0.8 rpm?

options.label: To generate power from sunlight
To help control systematic error in the anisotropy measurement
To keep its antenna pointed toward Earth
To cool the helium supply faster

items.explain: The need to control systematic error in the anisotropy measurement, and to measure the zodiacal cloud at different angles, called for the spin rate.

items.prompt: Why did designers choose a Sun-synchronous orbit that follows the line between sunlight and darkness on Earth?

options.label: To keep Earth and Sun below the shield for full sky scans
To fly directly above the Sun at local noon
To stay well inside the Earth's radiation belts
To greatly reduce the fuel costs it needed

items.explain: The orbit and spin axis kept the Earth and Sun below the plane of the shield, allowing a full sky scan every six months.

items.prompt: COBE was the second satellite built to study the background. Which one came just before it?

options.label: WMAP
Planck
RELIKT-1
The Infrared Astronomical Satellite

items.explain: COBE was the second cosmic microwave background satellite, following RELIKT-1, and was followed by WMAP and Planck.
